season.evidence: Guides advise early-mid September for the best glacier conditions at Tin Can Gap, with July and high-snow years forcing detours; logged ascents of the mountain peak Aug-Sep. Stored late July-Sep kept.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Sep 27 summit track ends at the lookout South Peak (about 120 m from our Middle pin, 450 m from our North pin); no report, no logged route name. The lookout line is stored as its own route.
Backdoor/Meadow Mountain approach to the lookout South Peak.
Backdoor bushwhack to the lookout.
SAR route to the lookout.
Backdoor then standard trail to the lookout.
Goat Flats trail to the lookout; report mentions ladders.
Meadow Mountain approach to lookout ladders.
Report goes to the lookout via Tupso Pass.
Oct 2009 trail trip to the lookout, off-season too.
March turn-around.

facts.text: Black bears with cubs were seen on the trail near Goat Flats in mid-August; store food carefully.
Water at Saddle Lake is poor; a better stream runs about halfway from there to Goat Flats, and melt streams are good beyond Tin Can Gap in late summer.
Late August into September is the usual window to dodge the moat and most glacier work below the Tin Can Gap shoulder.
